scoring_justification: Recomputing DFT energies from raw log files is infeasible in the verifier sandbox; the checker compares the agent's reported computed properties to the paper's hidden reference values within established tolerances.

hidden_assets.purpose: Paper-reported BDE, IE, EA, HOMO, LUMO for six compounds (Tables 2, 3 and Figure 7), plus derived RIE/REA and best antioxidant compound, used as hidden gold for comparison.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: RSC Advances paper DOI:10.1039/d0ra00903b, Tables 2 and 3, Figure 7
hidden_assets.generation_method: Values extracted from published tables and figures. RIE and REA computed from those values using public reference values (IE_Na=118.5, EA_F=78.4).
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: All numbers are the paper's own reported computational results for the specified level of theory; they are not invented.

schema.description: Each key is a compound name. Value is an object with: 'bde' (list of floats; kcal/mol), 'adiabatic_IE' (float; kcal/mol), 'adiabatic_EA' (float; kcal/mol), 'HOMO_energy' (float; eV), 'LUMO_energy' (float; eV).

outputs.description: Antioxidant thermochemical properties and frontier orbital energies computed at B3LYP/6-311++G(d,p)//B3LYP/6-31G(d) level for six polyaniline and polyaniline-fullerene compounds.

schema.description: 'compounds' is an object with compound name keys, each containing 'RIE' (float) and 'REA' (float). 'best_antioxidant' is a string naming the compound in the best antioxidant sector.

outputs.description: Full‑electron donor–acceptor map indices derived from IE/EA, plus identification of the best antioxidant compound.

output_contract.notes: The hidden checker compares the reported BDE, IE, EA, HOMO, LUMO, RIE, REA, and best_antioxidant against the paper's reported values with appropriate tolerances. Only typical chemical accuracy is expected; differences arising from the choice of open‑source DFT implementation are absorbed by the tolerances.
